newsitem.title: ESTONIA: REPORT SAYS TALLINNA HAD LIGUIDITY PROBLEMS.
newsitem.headline: REPORT SAYS TALLINNA HAD LIGUIDITY PROBLEMS.

text.p: Tallinna Pank defaulted in a payment of 50 million kroons on May 13 and borrowed on the overnight market at a high interest rate to resolve the liquidity crises, Aripaev newspaper said on Friday.
The bank had to transfer 45 million kroons before May 13 but did not have the cash on hand, Martti Siimann, the bank's financial markets director, was quoted as saying.
The bank had to borrow money at an exorbitant rate from the local overnight market to meet the central bank's minimum reserve requirements, which is 25 million kroons at the end of every banking day.
Tallinna Pank was 3.6 million kroons short and borrowed the sum from Hansabank at a rate of 10.25 percent, about six basis points above the average rate.
The move pushed up the one-week overnight average interest lending rate TALIBOR by 0.93 basis points on Wednesday to 5.43 percent.
Siimann said the loss was smaller than the interest rate of 15 percent it would have had to pay to the central bank.
Hansabank and Uhispank also said Tallinna Pank has been unstable in managing its liquidity.
Aripaev added that the bank had restored its liquidity by Thursday.
Tallinna Pank will also obtain a subordinated loan of 40 million kroons on May 20 and a syndicated loan of 400 million kroons on May 23.
It also set up a liquidity reserve of 25 million kroons compared to 10-20 million kroons earlier.
Tallinna Pank is scheduled to give a news conference today at 0900 GMT on its present situation and future plans.
Tallinna Pank chairman Rait Luukas said in a statement on Friday that the bank does not have problems with liquidity and that payments are being made regularly.
